bugs.what: The ending epilogue states 'You backed Tamsin on the barrow doors, sealed for the living's sake' — but I explicitly chose 'leave the doors open to the sky' for the Vale's barrow (confirmed by the game itself: 'You leave the doors open to the sky... Quest done: The Barrow Doors'). The epilogue appears to conflate that separate, already-resolved choice with an unrelated, vaguely-worded companion-dialogue line ('back her — a door that holds') said to Tamsin at Cinderhall about the Hundred Gallery mine, and mislabels it as the barrow.
bugs.where: The Hollow Throne (ending epilogue) / Ironbound Chapterhouse (Tamsin dialogue, 'back her — a door that holds')

bugs.what: Quest 'The Slag-Hound' (bearings: 'three north of the head-frame, then three east, where the downs open into the flooded quarry') marked itself done after I killed a generic wandering 'slag-hound' at just 3-north/0-east (The Long Spoil), well before reaching the actual den. The real den, 3 tiles further east at the Flooded Quarry, still held fresh scat, claw marks, and its own separately-named 'a scarred slag-hound' to fight — meaning the quest's own bearings pointed to real, distinct content the completion trigger didn't require visiting.
bugs.where: The Long Spoil (Iron Downs) / quest 'The Slag-Hound'

bugs.what: At the Hollow Throne, 'weigh the doors of the seat' reports 'No oil yet: the Ironbound keep casks at Cinderhall, and the palace has its own' and the burn option never appears — despite my carrying an item literally named 'cask of cinder-oil' (from Factor Corrin at Emberfall) the whole time. Nothing earlier disclosed that this oil was single-location-bound to the Emberfall chapel rather than a generic reusable resource.
bugs.where: The Hollow Throne (Marrowgate) / carried item 'cask of cinder-oil'

bugs.what: Preceptor Aldous's dialogue option 'press him on the Hundred' lists its cost as 'a miss costs standing with the Ironbound,' implying success is free — but succeeding the check also applied '(the Ironbound -1)' alongside the success text, an unstated cost on the winning outcome.
bugs.where: The Ironbound Chapterhouse (Cinderhall) / 'press him on the Hundred' dialogue

bugs.what: Glasswick's top-level room description stayed stuck on 'Word from the mother-house reached the priory' for several turns and multiple room visits after I fully resolved that plot thread with Prior Wenlock ('Quest done: Glasswick, After').

The Cinderhall 'hall's claim' political thread (started via 'back the hall's claim (Free Companies)' / '(the Watch)' with Ness at the head-frame) never surfaced its own resolution scene in Cinderhall itself — I only learned it had concluded from an offhand line at Wardmoor's Captain-General's Hall ('A Watch clerk sits at Cinderhall's chapterhouse desk now, backing the miners' hall'), so a player who never travels to Wardmoor would never see this thread pay off.
bugs.where: The Head-Frame (Cinderhall) quest hook / payoff only visible at The Captain-General's Hall (Wardmoor)

bugs.what: Scholar-tagged options that read as complete actions (e.g. 'read the founding outright (as a Scholar)' at Wardmoor's record-house) only unlocked flavor lore and left the actual mechanical action (opening the sealed shelf) still gated behind a separate persuade/pry/break check — the Scholar tag implied more resolution than it delivered.
bugs.where: The Record-House (Wardmoor) / 'read the founding outright' vs 'persuade her to open the shelf'

bugs.what: Failed skill checks (e.g. Quartermaster Bray's tally-error check, Preceptor Aldous's 'press him' check) can simply be retried immediately with no in-fiction consequence beyond spending another turn, which removes most tension from a stated 'DC' system — a bad roll is never actually a setback, just a delay.
bugs.where: The Quartermaster's Wagon (Camp Gallows) / 'find the error in his tally'

bugs.what: The distinction between a hollow being 'rested' vs 'bargained' (two separately tracked counters, 'Hollows rested: 3/8' and 'Hollows bargained: 1/8') is never explained at the point of choice — 'ring the recovered chapel bell' at Emberfall is only labeled '(settles this hold's grief: a bargain)' with no indication this is mechanically weaker than 'rest' until NPCs afterward volunteer 'quieter, not rested.'
bugs.where: The Roofless Chapel (Emberfall) / 'ring the recovered chapel bell'

bugs.what: 'Crypts of the dead laid to rest: 1/4' appears for the first time only on the final end-game status screen, with no earlier mention anywhere of this being a tracked stat or what the other three crypts are/where they are.

confusions: During the post-Aldous conversation with Tamsin, choosing 'back her — a door that holds' read as generic emotional support, not as a binding decision about whether the Hundred Gallery mine stays sealed — yet it swung Brother Osk's regard by -2 on the spot and the ending epilogue treats it as a permanent, recorded outcome.

Score reached its full displayed maximum (366/366) at turn ~475, after finishing only Act I plus 3 of 8 Act II holds, which can read as 'I've done everything' even though five holds, several companion questlines (Fenmarch, Hollowbrook, Saltkerns), and most of Marrowgate's city content were still untouched. (The game's own intro text does caveat this — 'it can fill long before the tale ends' — so this is a soft confusion, not a broken promise.)

The reeve's 'promise to seal the barrow' vs 'decline' choice at Last Light is framed as a real commitment with Watch consequences, but the priest's blessing overrides it minutes later regardless of the answer ('the stone doors grind open. No promise binds them shut'), so the early choice felt inert until the throne — by design, but the sequencing makes the intervening promise/decline dialogue feel like a no-op in the moment.

It's never made clear in advance which carried consumable items (like cask of cinder-oil, or the bell-clapper/bell pairing) are meant to combine with a specific later location versus being generic reusable resources; discovering the cinder-oil didn't count at the Hollow Throne was the only signal.
suggestions: Only complete bearings-based hunt quests (e.g. The Slag-Hound) when the player actually reaches the named den/location, not on any incidental same-species kill along the way.
Recognize location-bound consumables like cask of cinder-oil at other 'burn it' checkpoints, or tell the player up front that it's single-use for one specific site.

Refresh a town's headline room description as soon as the quest that changed it resolves, instead of leaving stale text like 'Word from the mother-house reached the priory' after the thread is closed.
Give politically-flavored side threads (like Cinderhall's miners'-hall claim) their own on-screen resolution beat at the hold where they started, not only a rumor line delivered elsewhere.
Flag world-state-altering companion-dialogue choices (like 'back her — a door that holds') with the same clarity as other big decisions, so a regard-swinging answer doesn't read as small talk.
Fix the ending epilogue's barrow-door line so it reflects the player's actual recorded choice (open vs sealed) instead of a different, unrelated 'door' decision.
Add a short one-line distinction between 'rest' and 'bargain' outcomes directly in the menu option text, rather than only revealing the gap through later NPC commentary.
Surface 'Crypts of the dead laid to rest' (and any other end-game-only counters) somewhere during play, not just on the final status screen, so a completionist player knows to look for them.
